content: 1. The Statement of Investigator, also known as Form FDA 1572, is a legally binding document signed by the clinical investigator. 2. The purpose of Form FDA 1572 is twofold: Second, it informs the investigator of their regulatory obligations and secures their commitment to adhere to FDA regulations. Investigators must complete the form accurately, as providing false information is a criminal offense under U.S. law (18 U.S.C. 1001). Deliberate falsification can also lead to disqualification from conducting clinical research. 3. Investigators must complete and sign Form FDA 1572 before participating in a clinical investigation under an Investigational New Drug (IND) application. The investigator should only sign the form after receiving sufficient information about the study, including the protocol and investigator’s brochure, and understanding the commitments outlined in Section 9 of the form. The signature affirms the investigator’s qualifications and their agreement to comply with FDA regulations. 4. If the investigator is not a physician, a qualified physician or dentist must be listed as a subinvestigator to oversee medical or dental decisions related to the trial. 5. The FDA does not specify minimum qualifications for investigators. Sponsors are responsible for selecting investigators with appropriate training and experience, which typically includes familiarity with human subject protection (HSP) regulations, Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards, and FDA regulations for clinical studies. 6. Form FDA 1572 does not need to be submitted to the FDA. However, sponsors are required to collect the form from investigators. Some sponsors choose to submit it to the FDA because it consolidates information required under 21 CFR 312.23(a)(6)(iii)(b). 7. A new Form FDA 1572 must be completed and signed when a new protocol is added to the IND or when a new investigator joins the study. For other changes, such as updates to the IRB address or the addition of subinvestigators, the investigator should document the changes in study records and inform the sponsor. The form itself does not need to be revised unless required by the sponsor. 8. Investigators are not required to sign Form FDA 1572 for studies not conducted under an IND or for medical device studies. For device studies, sponsors must obtain a signed investigator agreement containing similar information. 9. Sponsors are not required to conduct foreign clinical studies under an IND. If a foreign study is conducted under an IND, it must comply with all FDA IND requirements unless a waiver is granted. If the study is not conducted under an IND, it must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 312.120 if the data will be submitted to the FDA. 10. Investigators conducting foreign clinical studies under an IND must sign Form FDA 1572. If the study is not conducted under an IND, the investigator is not required to sign the form. If local laws prohibit signing the form, the site may operate as a non-IND site, and the study must comply with 21 CFR 312.120 if the data will be used for FDA submissions. 11. Investigators conducting foreign studies under an IND must comply with local laws and regulations in addition to FDA requirements. Sponsors should obtain written commitments from investigators to adhere to local laws. 12. If a foreign investigator cannot meet all requirements of Form FDA 1572, such as IRB membership, the sponsor may request a waiver from the FDA. The waiver request should describe alternative mechanisms for ensuring human subject protection, such as using an Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) that complies with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards. If granted, the waiver letter should be attached to the signed Form FDA 1572. 13. Foreign investigators complying with ICH E6 Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines generally meet FDA IND requirements, except for differences in IRB membership and informed consent regulations. Sponsors may request waivers for these differences. If conflicts arise, the FDA is open to discussing resolutions on a case-by-case basis. 14. Multinational studies may include U.S. sites under an IND and foreign sites not under an IND. Investigators at U.S. sites and foreign sites under the IND must sign Form FDA 1572. Foreign sites not under the IND are not required to sign the form. Sponsors should discuss plans to pool data from U.S. and foreign sites with the FDA if the data will be used for marketing approval. 15. Sponsors can submit data from foreign studies not conducted under an IND to support U.S. clinical investigations or marketing approval. Submissions should clearly indicate compliance with 21 CFR 312.120, and supporting documentation must meet the requirements outlined in 21 CFR 312.120(b). 16. A new Form FDA 1572 does not need to be prepared or signed when the OMB expiration date is reached. 17. Both double-sided and two-page versions of Form FDA 1572 are acceptable. 18. Form FDA 1572 can be completed electronically or by hand. Typed forms are preferred for legibility. The form must be signed and dated by the investigator, either by hand or using an acceptable electronic method. 19. The investigator’s full legal name should be entered in Section 1 of Form FDA 1572. Titles, degrees, or professional qualifications may be included after the legal name. 20. The address entered in Section 1 should be the investigator’s work or business address, where they can be reached by mail or in person. 21. Co-investigators must sign separate Form FDA 1572s, as each is considered an investigator under FDA regulations. It is acceptable to have more than one investigator at a single site. 22. Section 2 of Form FDA 1572 requires the investigator to attach a curriculum vitae (CV) or other statement of qualifications, demonstrating their expertise in conducting the clinical investigation. 23. CVs or statements of qualifications do not need to be updated during a clinical study. 24. CVs are not required to be signed or dated. The investigator’s signature on Form FDA 1572 attests to the accuracy of the submitted CV or qualifications. 25. Section 3 of Form FDA 1572 should list the addresses of all locations where the clinical investigation will be conducted, including where test articles will be shipped if different from the investigator’s address. 26. Research facilities listed in Section 3 include locations where study activities are conducted, such as healthcare facilities, laboratories, or storage sites for test articles. 27. If an investigator conducts study activities at multiple sites, all site addresses should be listed in Section 3. However, subjects’ home addresses do not need to be listed if the protocol allows for home-based procedures. 28. Section 4 of Form FDA 1572 should list clinical laboratories or testing facilities directly supporting the study, such as diagnostic labs or pharmacokinetic analysis labs. 29. Only the primary laboratory needs to be listed in Section 4 if it can trace samples to satellite or contract labs. 30. The IRB reviewing the study does not need to be located at the research site. Independent or centralized IRBs are acceptable as long as they meet FDA requirements. 31. Subinvestigators listed in Section 6 are individuals who make direct and significant contributions to the study data, such as performing protocol-required procedures or collecting data. 32. Nurses, residents, or office staff providing ancillary or intermittent care do not need to be listed in Section 6 unless they make significant contributions to the study data. 33. Pharmacists and research coordinators should be listed in Section 6 if they make direct and significant contributions to the study data. For example, research coordinators often recruit subjects, collect data, and maintain study records, so they are typically included. 34. Subinvestigators are not required to submit statements of qualifications. 35. Subinvestigators listed in Section 6 must disclose financial interests under 21 CFR Part 54. This includes the investigator’s spouse and dependent children. 36. Section 7 of Form FDA 1572 should list the name and code number of all protocols under the IND that the investigator will conduct. 37. For phase 4 studies, the investigator should identify the study as postmarketing in Section 7 but does not need to mark the boxes in Section 8. 38. For phase 2 or 3 studies, the investigator must submit the full protocol or a detailed description. For phase 1 studies, an outline is sufficient.
